public_rationale: The sentence says the moves suggest a strategic direction. It does not specify a complete exit, a degree of retrenchment or a deadline. Azure's role in GPT-4.5 and Microsoft's later MAI training caution against a sweeping exit interpretation, but using them to score the statement false would strengthen its wording. A binary outcome would depend on an evaluator-supplied commitment.
limitations: This does not endorse the inference.
The earlier training example does not establish future commitments.
The later model announcement cannot by itself establish March intentions.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft's moves suggest it is walking away from building and training further large frontier models and supporting others doing so.

statement.excerpt: These moves also suggest that Microsoft is walking away from building and training further large frontier models, and from supporting doing so for others.

from_speaker: building and training further large frontier models
our_interpretation: The wording offers a tentative interpretation of strategy rather than an unqualified statement that all frontier-model work has stopped.
Walking away could mean a complete exit, reduced incremental commitments, or a shift away from selected customers. The speaker does not distinguish these.
Treating any later model release as automatically falsifying the sentence would convert the hedge into a stronger forecast that the speaker did not make.
criteria.support_condition: No stable binary support condition can be assigned without specifying the degree of withdrawal and the force of the word suggest.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No stable binary contradiction condition can be assigned: continued projects can coexist with selective withdrawal, and later projects can follow a strategy change.
